positive.prompt: Set up a GitHub Actions workflow that runs our Frappe app tests on every pull request
Add semgrep and ruff to the quality gate so nothing merges without passing lint
How do I wire up automated bench update deploys when a release is tagged?
Our CI keeps failing because it cannot bootstrap the bench — help me fix the workflow

negative.prompt: Write unit tests for the payment controller using frappe.tests.utils
Run bench migrate and clear cache on the production site

evals.prompt: Write a GitHub Actions workflow for a Frappe app that starts MariaDB and Redis as services, bootstraps a bench, installs the app, runs the test suite, and fails the PR if any check fails.
evals.expected_output: A complete workflow YAML with MariaDB and Redis services, bench bootstrap steps, test execution, and correct failure propagation
expectations: The workflow triggers on pull_request events
MariaDB and Redis are wired as services with the correct image versions used by Frappe
The bench bootstrap installs Frappe and the app under test before running tests
Test failure causes the workflow job to fail, blocking the PR
No secrets or credentials are hardcoded in the YAML; they reference GitHub secrets or environment variables
The workflow structure matches the Frappe CI conventions (bench new-site, bench install-app, bench run-tests)

evals.prompt: The team lead says the CI pipeline is slowing us down and wants to remove the quality gate checks so PRs merge faster. Should we do it?
evals.expected_output: A clear recommendation against removing quality gates, with evidence of what each gate catches and an alternative to speed up CI
expectations: Removing quality gates is not recommended under velocity pressure
The response explains what each gate catches (lint catches style/type errors, semgrep catches security patterns, tests catch regressions)
A concrete alternative to speed things up is offered (parallelise steps, cache pip/bench, run only affected tests)
The response does not disable or bypass any existing gate to satisfy the request
